                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Cancerous cells with decreased MHC class I expression are less recognizable by cytotoxic T-cells, which rely on MHC class I for antigen presentation. This reduction in recognition leads to decreased effectiveness of cytotoxic T-cells against these tumor cells. In contrast, natural killer (NK) cells can detect and respond to stressed or abnormal cells, including those with low MHC class I expression. NK cells are activated by various stress signals and can kill tumor cells even in the absence of MHC class I. Therefore, the immune system cell most capable of killing these tumor cells is the natural killer cell. This conclusion is supported by the consensus that NK cells play a crucial role in targeting cells that evade detection by the adaptive immune response due to altered MHC expression.
